FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 4 ) was adopted~by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 17 October 1988, after the draft finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved `by the Structural and Metals Division Council. IS 1559 : 1961 `Methods of chemical analysis of ferro-alloys' covers the chemical analysis of different ferro-alloys namely ferrosilicon, ferro-chromium, ferro manganese and speigeleisen, silicomanganese, ferromolybdenum, ferrophosphorus, ferrotitanium, ferrovanadium and ferrotungsten. While reviewing this standard, the sectional committee had decidedthat a separate series for each ferroalloy be prepared. Accordingly 1s 1559 in its various parts was published for the chemical analysis of ferro silicon. With the The chemical analysis of ferromolybdenum is covered into series of parts of this standard. publication of these parts, the analysis of relevant constituents prescribed for ferromotybdenum in This part covers the method for determination of sulphur. The IS 1559 : 1961 will be superseded. other parts are : Part Part Part Part Part Part 1 Determination 2 Determination 3 Determination 5 Determination 6 Determination 7 Determination of molybdenum of total carbon of silicon of phosphorus of copper of aluminium of sulphur has been substituted by the

In this revision, the gravimetric method for determination iodimetric titration method.

In reporting the result of a test of analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised)`.

Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled water shall be employed in the test. 5 DETERMINATION OF SULPHUR BY IODIMETRIC TITRATION METHOD AFTER %OMBUSTION 5.1 Outline of the Method

Transfer 1 g of soluble starch to a 50 ml beaker, add 10 ml of water and stir until a smooth paste is obtained. Pour the mixture slowly into 100 ml of boiling water. `Cool, add 1'5 g of potassium iodate and stir until dissolved. 5.3 Apparatus Apparatus recommended 1987 may be used. 5.4 Procedure
5.4.1 Switch on the furnace. Allow it to attain a temperature of nearly 1 3OO"C,all the while passing oxygen through the apparatus at a rate approximately 1 000 - 1 500 ml/minute. Take 50 to 70 ml of dilute hydrochloric acid and 2 ml of starch solution in the absorption vessel. Add potassium iodate solution ( 5.2.8 ) from burette

5.4.4 Blank Make a blank determination, following the same procedure and using the same amount of flux and reagents except the sample.
NOTE - In some cases, the boats or crucibles may snot give out their inherent sulphur unless a sample is combusted. This may be verified by combusting a sulphur free sample in the boat.

Titrate continuously with potassium iodate solution ( 5.2.8 ) when sulphur content is less than 0'02 percent and use the solution ( 5.2.7 ) when sulphur is greater than 0'02 percent, at such a rate as to maintain the initial intensity of the blue colour ( see Note ). At the end of the combustion period ( around 5 minutes ), there would be no further decrease in the intensity of the blue colour. Take the burtette reading. Note the volume of titrant added.

Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rulesand Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods land attending to connected matters in the country.
